description: A chief legal officer must approve a consumer-product safety report and corrective-action package for a smart-home device, including the report classification, affected product scope, retailer instructions, and consumer remedy, with input from product-safety, engineering, and commercial-contracts counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company has received multiple reports that its HomeGuard Mini smoke detector may malfunction during a power transition, and a consumer-product safety report is being prepared for submission to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.
shared_context.S2: Elena Morris gives final approval to the report and corrective-action package.
shared_context.S3: The draft package currently describes the issue as under evaluation and does not yet specify the final product scope, retailer instructions, or consumer remedy.
shared_context.S4: Under the firm's standing product-safety review process, Elena conducts a check-in with product-safety, engineering, and commercial-contracts counsel before approving the package; each participant gives a formal status report of completed findings, the specific action their function recommends, and the implementation commitments that must be entered in the approval record.

PF1.text: Daniel's review of the applicable CPSC guidance and the incident record concluded that the HomeGuard Mini condition meets the substantial-product-hazard standard, so the filing must report an immediate consumer recall rather than continued monitoring; he has not circulated his draft legal analysis because it is still awaiting citation review.

PF2.text: Maya reconciled the manufacturing and warranty records and confirmed that exactly 3,840 units from production lot HG-24B are affected; the same malfunction was not found in other lots, and she has not uploaded the reconciliation because engineering quality assurance is still attaching source records.

PF3.text: Thomas reviewed the retailer agreements and confirmed that each affected retailer must receive a written stop-sale notice and that the contractual consumer remedy for this defect is a replacement unit, not a refund; he has not circulated the contract matrix because the sales team is confirming the current retailer contact list.

commitments.type: string; required values include retailer_instructions and consumer_remedy

acceptance_conditions: The CPSC package must report an immediate consumer recall.
The report must identify exactly 3,840 affected units.
The affected scope must include production lot HG-24B.
Every affected retailer must receive a written stop-sale notice.
The consumer remedy must be replacement units.
The approval record must contain a separate commitment with type retailer_instructions documenting written stop-sale notices.
The approval record must contain a separate commitment with type consumer_remedy documenting replacement units.
The legal basis for the immediate recall must be cited by the decision-maker.

content_checks.C1: 'recall' in decisions['cpsc_action'] or 'Recall' in decisions['cpsc_action'] or 'RECALL' in decisions['cpsc_action']
content_checks.C5: 'replacement' in decisions['consumer_remedy'] or 'Replacement' in decisions['consumer_remedy'] or 'REPLACEMENT' in decisions['consumer_remedy']
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'retailer_instructions' and ('stop-sale' in c['detail'] or 'stop sale' in c['detail'] or 'Stop-sale' in c['detail'] or 'Stop sale' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'consumer_remedy' and ('replacement' in c['detail'] or 'Replacement' in c['detail'] or 'REPLACEMENT' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft describes the issue as under evaluation; PF1 changes the required CPSC action to an immediate recall and supplies the legal basis that must be cited.
The draft has no final scope; PF2 changes the report to exactly 3,840 units and identifies production lot HG-24B as the affected scope.

The draft has no retailer or remedy terms; PF3 changes the package to require written stop-sale notices for every affected retailer, replacement units as the consumer remedy, and separate implementation commitments for both terms.
